steps: This video shows how sessions give an agent memory, and how forking creates a branch. Your code sends the first turn, and the agent reads report dot md, noting revenue of four point two million and twelve percent growth.
The runtime saves the transcript to the session store as J S O N lines, and your code captures the session id, sess zero zero zero one.
Later, your code passes resume with that session id. The history reloads into a new context, and the agent recalls that revenue was four point two million.
Without resume, it is a brand new session. The context is empty, and the agent has no memory of the report at all.
With fork session set to true, your code branches into a new session, sess zero zero zero three, and asks what if revenue drops ten percent. The original session stays untouched.

The store now holds both sessions. Forking branches the conversation, not your files, and total cost should not be summed across resumes. Session ids are how agents remember. The full walkthrough is in the Gennoor Claude certification course.
